newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian police lift cordon, let students march.
newsitem.headline: Serbian police lift cordon, let students march.

text.p: Serbian riot police on Monday lifted a cordon that had blocked student pro-democracy protesters from marching for over a week and let them roam around the centre of Belgrade, witnesses said.

Thousands of students, who have been holding a non-stop rally in the city for more than eight days, marched jubilantly around the city, shouting "let's go for a walk" and blowing whistles, the witnesses said.
They said the police withdrew the cordon at about 4 a.m. (0300 GMT).

The move marked a major concession by the Socialist authorities. President Slobodan Milosevic's government has largely ignored demands by the students and the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition to reinstate annulled local election results last November.

The students, demonstrating 24-hours a day in the bitter cold of the Balkan winter, have kept up their spirits with speeches, dancing to rock music, and by playing stunts such as getting women students to kiss the policemen.
The Serbian church, siding with the protesters, planned to lead a religious procession through Belgrade later on Monday.
